findings.claim: Task 10's check explicitly accepts a native <input type="submit"> as the submit control (structure.test.mjs line 117 selects '.signup-form button, .signup-form input[type="submit"]'), but Task 8 collects every '.signup-form input' (line 49) and asserts exactly 3 (line 56). A learner who completes Task 10 with <input type="submit" value="Request a spot">, a valid native submit button, therefore fails Task 8 with the misleading message 'Keep the three sign-up inputs with their ids from the starter.', even though the three text inputs are unchanged and correctly labelled. With every task now required, this false fail blocks lab completion for a correct alternative.

evidence.section: Executed in scratch copy $TMPDIR/pep-rf-sme/html-and-css (npm ci; Playwright 1.55.1 Chromium): private completion passes 11/11; replacing only the <button type="submit"> with <input type="submit" value="Request a spot"> gives task 7 pass, task 8 FAIL ('Keep the three sign-up inputs with their ids from the starter.'), task 9 pass, task 10 pass.

MDN, <input type="submit">, retrieved 2026-11-10T06:37:57Z: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/input/submit - intro: '<input> elements of type submit are rendered as buttons.'

MDN, HTMLInputElement.labels, retrieved 2026-11-10T06:37:57Z: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLInputElement/labels - 'returns a NodeList of the <label> elements associated with the <input> element' (a submit input has none, and the count check fires first).

findings.recommendation: Scope Task 8's collection to the three fields (for example '#hiker-name, #hiker-email, #group-size', or '.signup-form input:not([type=submit]):not([type=button]):not([type=reset])'), or, if only <button> is intended, drop input[type="submit"] from Task 10's selector and say 'a <button> element' in the README Task 10 outcome. Rerun the solved run afterwards.
